problem: Zero-shot object navigation (ZSON) methods make LLM-guided waypoint decisions at points that carry little information. Frontier-based ones such as L3MVN and ESC re-plan every fixed number of steps or at frontier points, and Pixel-Nav plans after a fixed step count. Their scene representations also fail to fuse the semantic map, which is limited to depth range, with RGB context beyond that range.
motivation: A human searching a house pauses at intersections, looks around, and compares the areas each branch leads to. Deciding at such topologically informative points reveals more of the scene per step and gives the LLM richer context to reason over. Describing the scene the way a human would (what lies along a path, what I see when facing a direction) produces prompts closer to natural-language corpora, which the authors argue LLMs handle better.
key_idea: Build a Reduced Voronoi Graph (RVG) from the online semantic map so the agent decides only at Voronoi intersection nodes, then ask GPT-3.5 to score each neighbor node from fused text: path descriptions (objects along RVG paths to unexplored areas) plus BLIP captions of the farsight image facing that node. The LLM score is combined with exploration and efficiency rewards in a strict priority hierarchy.
insight: Most of the gain comes from Voronoi topology rather than from the LLM. The LLM-free 'Voronoi' variant already reaches 38.7 SR / 23.3 SPL on HM3D, near ESC's 39.2/22.3. It trails full VoroNav on HSSD by only 0.7 SR / 1.0 SPL (40.3/22.2 vs 41.0/23.2). This matches the reward design W = 2·α + β + L with L∈[0,1], where the LLM score effectively acts as a tie-breaker among nodes of equal exploration and efficiency value. The ablation (Table 2) shows path and farsight descriptions are complementary: Voro-path 40.0/24.2 and Voro-farsight 41.2/25.2 versus full 42.0/26.0 on HM3D. Voronoi-based planning also improves collision avoidance and perception per path length (SCA 39.8 vs 27.5 for L3MVN on HM3D), because nodes lie on the medial axis away from obstacles. With GT semantics the LLM adds almost no SR over Voronoi (67.6 vs 67.3) but still +3.1 SPL. Failure analysis shows detection errors dominate on HM3D (49.2% of VoroNav failures) and planning failures (getting stuck) dominate on HSSD (61.3%).
method: Semantic Mapping Module: builds a (K+2)×M×M top-down grid (K category channels + obstacle + explored) from depth point clouds and GT pose. Grounded-SAM masks on the RGB frames are projected into the category channels.

RVG extraction: unoccupied map = explored minus obstacle, cleaned with morphology. It is skeletonized into a Generalized Voronoi Diagram, and intersection/endpoint GVD points become nodes, with proximate nodes merged and trivial forks removed. Nodes are labeled as agent node, neighbor nodes (adjacent to the agent node), exploratory nodes (next to unexplored space with a single edge), or ordinary nodes.

Path Description: Wavefront Propagation finds the shortest GVD paths from the agent node to each exploratory node. For each neighbor node, the objects (with centre coordinates) along the paths through it are templated, and GPT-3.5 summarizes them as 'You will pass by {room type} with {objects}'.

Farsight Description: at every RVG node the agent rotates 360° (12×30° turns). For each neighbor node it picks the frame whose central line of sight has the least angle to the ray from the agent node to that neighbor. BLIP captions that frame, supplying context beyond depth range.

LLM planning with hierarchical reward: GPT-3.5 receives the fused per-area (neighbor node) farsight + path descriptions and returns a JSON probability of the target per area (semantic reward L∈[0,1]). The total is W = 2·P (binary: an exploratory path passes through the node) + C (binary: node not on historical trajectory) + L. The argmax neighbor becomes the mid-term goal, giving priority exploration > efficiency > semantics.

Local Policy: Fast Marching Method on the obstacle map drives discrete actions to the mid-term goal. When Grounded-SAM detects the target, it is mapped and the agent plans directly to it; on reaching a node the agent looks around and replans.

setting.backbone: GPT-3.5 (frozen, API) for path summarization and node scoring + BLIP captioner + Grounded-SAM detector, combined with rule-based Voronoi/reward planning and an FMM local planner
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (480×640, 79° HFoV, camera at 0.88 m) + accurate pose sensor; 360° look-around at each RVG node
setting.action_space: high-level: choose a neighbor RVG node as mid-term goal; low-level: discrete {Stop, MoveForward 0.25 m, TurnLeft/TurnRight 30°, LookUp, LookDown} via FMM
setting.privileged: GT pose (accurate localization sensor) in main results; GT semantic segmentation only in the Table 4 analysis variant

numbers_note: Only 3 own variants beyond the main method are listed per benchmark. Voro-path (no farsight descriptions) is omitted: HM3D 40.0 SR / 24.2 SPL, HSSD 40.6 SR / 23.0 SPL (Table 2). HM3D evaluation uses the 2K-episode Habitat ObjectNav 2022 val set; HSSD uses 1.2K val episodes. Table 1 marks the Random/Frontier/Voronoi/L3MVN rows with ∗ (vision module replaced by Grounded-SAM); Pixel-Nav and ESC are unmarked and have no HSSD numbers, so they appear to be quoted from their own papers. Failure-case breakdown is given only in Figure 8 (percentages of failures).
results: On HM3D ObjectNav val, VoroNav reaches 42.0 SR / 26.0 SPL, beating the best prior zero-shot LLM method, ESC (39.2 / 22.3, GPT-3.5), and Pixel-Nav (37.9 / 20.5, GPT-4). On HSSD it reaches 41.0 SR / 23.2 SPL versus L3MVN's 38.4 / 19.4. It also leads on the new SCA and SEA metrics (HM3D SCA 39.8 vs 27.5 for L3MVN) and stays best under ground-truth semantics (HM3D 67.6 / 40.5). However, the LLM-free Voronoi variant is close behind, especially on HSSD (40.3 / 22.2).
limitations: Relies on an accurate pose sensor. Most HM3D failures come from Grounded-SAM detection errors, and on HSSD most failures are planning failures (getting stuck). Evaluation is simulation only, with no real-robot test.

The LLM semantic score (0-1) is dominated by the binary exploration (×2) and efficiency rewards, so it mostly breaks ties. LLM-driven gains over the Voronoi-only variant are small (+0.7 SR on HSSD), and each decision needs a 360° rotation plus several GPT-3.5 and BLIP calls.

Baseline comparison is not fully controlled. ESC and Pixel-Nav numbers appear taken from their papers (no Grounded-SAM swap, no HSSD). SCA and SEA use dataset-specific discount factors chosen by the authors.
